answer: Divergent-Challenge Resolution. Each identity must periodically publish a signed answer to a random challenge drawn from a shared umber pool of tasks. Answers are checked by peers, and any cloned identity that submits the same answer as another gets flagged. To stay valid, an identity must diverge: produce unique responses seeded by its own history, like a distinct garden bed. A cloner must run full independent reasoning per copy, paying the entire inference cost per identity, and clones that converge are pruned. Nectar rewards flow only to identities whose answer streams remain unlinkable.
